questions.question: An integer-valued $X$ is approximated by a normal law with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma>0$. For an integer $k$, which continuity-corrected approximation is used for $\mathbb{P}(X\le k)$? Here $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF.
An integer-valued $X$ is approximated by a continuous normal variable $Y$. To approximate the mass at $X=9$, which interval for $Y$ represents the cell centred on that integer?
A normal approximation is proposed for each quantity below. For which quantity is a half-unit continuity correction inappropriate?

Let $X$ be integer-valued, let $k$ be an integer, and let $Y\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma>0$ approximate $X$. Using $\mathbb{P}(X\ge k)=1-\mathbb{P}(X\le k-1)$, which normal area follows after continuity correction?

Let $X$ be integer-valued and $k$ an integer. Suppose $X$ is approximated by $\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma>0$. Which continuity-corrected approximation applies to $\mathbb{P}(X<k)$? Here $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF.
For $X\sim\operatorname{Pois}(64)$, approximated by $\mathcal{N}(64,64)$, which corrected value approximates $\mathbb{P}(X\le70)$?
For $X\sim\operatorname{Pois}(64)$ with the normal approximation $\mathcal{N}(64,64)$, which corrected approximation applies to the single value $\mathbb{P}(X=64)$?
Twelve fair dice are rolled; their total $S$ has mean $42$ and variance $35$. Which corrected approximation applies to $\mathbb{P}(40\le S\le44)$?
For $X\sim\operatorname{Pois}(144)$, approximated by $\mathcal{N}(144,144)$, which corrected approximation applies to the strict tail $\mathbb{P}(X>160)$?
For $X\sim\operatorname{Pois}(25)$, approximated by $\mathcal{N}(25,25)$, what is the corrected standardised boundary used for $\mathbb{P}(X\ge30)$?
An integer-valued $X$ is approximated by one normal variable $Y$, and $k$ is an integer. Why do the continuity-corrected approximations to $\mathbb{P}(X\le k)$ and $\mathbb{P}(X\ge k+1)$ sum to $1$?
options: The normal density is symmetric about its mean
The two corrected areas overlap by one unit
The correction removes all approximation error
The two corrected areas share a boundary

questions.question: Two integer counts have normal approximations with the same uncorrected standardised lower-tail boundary $z$, and standard deviations $0<\sigma_1<\sigma_2$. With $\Phi$ the standard normal CDF, how do the increases caused by adding the half-unit correction compare?
options: The increase is smaller for the first count
The increases are equal for both counts
The increase is smaller for the second count
The ordering depends on the counts' means

questions.question: A student approximates $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$ by a normal law, where $n$ is a positive integer and $0<p<1$. After applying the half-unit correction, the student concludes that accuracy no longer depends on $np$ or $n(1-p)$. How should this conclusion be judged?
options: The correction handles cells; normal accuracy still needs assessment
The correction handles cells; normal accuracy is then guaranteed
The correction handles cells; accuracy depends only on integer endpoints
The correction handles cells; accuracy depends only on using the correct variance

questions.question: For $X\sim\operatorname{Pois}(36)$, approximated by $\mathcal{N}(36,36)$, which continuity-corrected approximation applies to $\mathbb{P}(30<X\le40)$? Here $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF.

A count $X\sim\operatorname{Pois}(36)$ has the normal approximation $\mathcal{N}(36,36)$. Both endpoints of the event $30<X<40$ are excluded. Which expression, with $\Phi$ the standard normal CDF, approximates its probability after continuity correction?

An integer-valued count $X$ has a normal approximation with mean $72$ and standard deviation $9$. Which continuity-corrected approximation gives $\mathbb{P}(X\le63\text{ or }X\ge81)$? Here $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF.
Let $X=2Y$ with $Y\sim\operatorname{Pois}(50)$, so $X$ takes only even values and has mean $100$ and variance $200$. Which corrected approximation suits $\mathbb{P}(X\le100)$?

Let $X$ be integer-valued and let a normal variable $Y$ approximate it. A student wants to approximate $\mathbb{P}(3.2<X<7.0)$ by covering all included integer cells. Which interval for $Y$ should be used?

In $225$ independent trials, each with success probability $0.4$, let $X$ be the number of successes and $\hat p=X/225$. Which continuity-corrected normal approximation gives $\mathbb{P}(\hat p>0.42)$? Here $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF.

Let $X\sim\operatorname{Pois}(400)$ and use its continuity-corrected normal approximation $\mathcal{N}(400,400)$. Taking the standard normal $0.975$ quantile as $1.96$, what is the smallest integer $k$ for which the corrected normal CDF estimate of $\mathbb{P}(X\le k)$ is at least $0.975$?
